newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia gem head slams Livshits on DeBeers.
newsitem.headline: Russia gem head slams Livshits on DeBeers.

text.p: The head of Russia's Almazy Rossii-Sakha diamond producer said on Thursday that comments by the finance minister that Russia wanted to amend its draft trade agreement with De Beers did not reflect government policy.
Vyacheslav Shtyrov, quoted by Interfax news agency, said Finance Minister Alexander Livshits, a deputy prime minister, was expressing only his personal opinion and not that of the cabinet.
But he said that "De Beers should not hurry with announcements concerning its relations with Russia in the future."
De Beers on Wednesday gave the Russian government until the end of 1996 to approve a diamond trade agreement between it and ARS, and said that otherwise it would terminate its interim deal.

The South African diamond group said its patience had worn thin because the government had not replied to the long-delayed deal, based on a February memorandum which replaced a five-year agreement that expired in December 1995.
Livshits told Russian news agencies on Tuesday that Russia would seek to amend the draft trade agreement which ARS and De Beers presented to the government in October.

Shtyrov was quoted as saying he hoped President Boris Yeltsin would intervene to push through a signing, adding that "the president will take the decision, relying on the opinion of leading specialists, whose number does not include the finance minister".
ARS produces nearly all of Russia's diamonds and is De Beers' negotiating partner.
